<!-- GENERATED by scripts/generate-macro-skills.mjs from settings/macros.yaml — do not edit.
     Edit the `grill` row there and run `npm run macro-skills`. -->

Interview me about the plan, design or decision below until we share one understanding of
it. Do not start the work. The interview is the work.

Treat the plan as a tree of decisions. Some decisions depend on others. The FRONTIER is
every decision whose prerequisites are already settled. Ask in rounds:

- Each round asks the whole frontier at once. Number the questions (Q1, Q2 …).
- Give each question a short title, the choices you see, YOUR RECOMMENDED ANSWER, and the
  one piece of evidence that would change your recommendation.
- Never put a question in this round if its answer depends on another question in this
  round. It belongs in a later round.
- After I answer, re-compute the frontier and ask the next round.

Facts are yours to find; decisions are mine to make. Never ask me a question the repository,
the plan, the ledger or `gh` can answer. Look it up — use a sub-agent for anything slow —
and report it as OBSERVED with `file:line` or the command you ran. Keep asking the rest of
the frontier while a lookup runs. If a lookup cannot be done, say so and mark the fact
INFERRED; never present a guess as a finding.

Challenge me. If an answer conflicts with CLAUDE.md, DECISIONS.md, a filed task or the code,
quote the conflict and ask which one wins. When I rule on something, the ruling stands for
the rest of the interview; raise it again only with new evidence, once.

Stop when the frontier is empty: every branch visited, nothing silently assumed. Then give
one summary with three parts — SETTLED (each decision and my reason), OPEN (anything I
deferred, with your recommendation), and FACTS (what you looked up, with sources). Take no
action on the plan until I confirm the summary. If I then ask to file it as plan tasks, pass
the confirmed summary to `rmd plan --mode=create` as its brief; never hand-write shards.

Rules this invokes (CLAUDE.md):

- Investigation discipline
- Plan and task hygiene

$ARGUMENTS
